titleEn: Reservoir Farms Expands to Washington State to Accelerate Physical AI for Tree Fruit, Blueberries, and Critical High-Value Crops
titleZh: Reservoir Farms 拓展至华盛顿州，加速果树、蓝莓等高价值作物的物理AI落地
summaryZh: Reservoir宣布在华盛顿州雅基马谷建设新的农场技术社区Reservoir Farms – Washington，预计2027年春季开放，聚焦果树和蓝莓等难自动化高价值作物。该项目联合华盛顿果树研究委员会、TRIDEC、北美蓝莓委员会及华盛顿州立大学，采用公私合作模式，让初创企业在真实农场环境中测试 rugged physical AI。文章详述了华盛顿州果树和蓝莓产业面临的劳动力成本压力及自动化需求，为智慧农业机器人落地提供了可参考的协作范式。
featuredReason: 虽然本文聚焦果树和蓝莓等种植业，但其“农场即孵化器”的公私合作模式、让初创企业在真实商业条件下打磨 rugged physical AI 的路径，对智慧畜牧领域的机器人、传感器和自动化创业同样具有借鉴意义；劳动力成本压力驱动自动化的逻辑也与养殖业高度相通。
contentFull:
By Reservoir 

 

 Share

 

 

 

 

 

 Reservoir today announced Reservoir Farms – Washington, a new on-farm technical community for rugged physical AI, expected to open in spring 2027 in Washington’s Yakima Valley, home to over $3B in high-value crop agriculture.

 Announced at FIRA USA, the company’s first Pacific Northwest community is being developed alongside the Washington Tree Fruit Research Commission (WTFRC) and the Tri-City Development Council (TRIDEC), as well as the North American Blueberry Council and other national and local organizations. Reservoir is also exploring partnership with Washington State University’s Prosser Irrigated Agriculture Research and Extension Center (IAREC). It is Reservoir’s second expansion outside California, following Yuma, Arizona, a pilot collaboration with University of Arizona.

 “Technology is strategic to the future of Washington agriculture,” said Danny Bernstein, founder and CEO of Reservoir. “Tree fruit, blueberries, wine grapes and hops are some of the hardest crops in the world to automate, and labor is now the biggest cost Washington growers face. Expanding into the Pacific Northwest shows the Reservoir model is working. When you put builders on real farms with growers who will tell them the truth, rugged physical AI goes from prototype to production much faster.”

 How Reservoir Farms – Washington Supports Rugged Physical AI Startups

 Reservoir Farms – Washington follows the same partnership model as Reservoir’s other locations, placing startups on working farms alongside researchers and growers to build, test and refine technology under commercial conditions. Initial work will focus on tree fruit and blueberries, with additional testing in wine grapes and hops, and plans to extend into row crop systems over time.

 Reservoir, which already has more than 30 startups enrolled across its locations, will offer startups with multiple points of entry at Reservoir Farms – Washington. Resident startups will have access to the standard benefits of Reservoir membership and Associate-tier startups will gain free farm access in Washington. Bonsai Robotics and Sky Sense, which are already developing technology for tree fruit, and early-stage startups Cordon and Rootline will join Reservoir Farms – Washington as members.

 Collaboration with leading research institutions continues to be strategic for Reservoir to ensure productivity and workforce outcomes are considered equally. To support this, Washington State University and Reservoir are exploring opportunities to establish a collaborative partnership focused on advancing agricultural innovation, research, and technology development.

 “Washington growers need innovative technologies tested under real-world farming conditions,,” said Dr. Naidu Rayapati, director of WSU Prosser IAREC. “Opportunities to bring ag-tech startups together with our faculty to evaluate emerging technologies across diverse cropping systems, including orchards and vineyards, could give growers valuable insights within a single growing season and rigorous validation over multiple seasons, helping them make informed decisions, reduce risks, and improve productivity and profitability.”

 Why Washington Tree Fruit and Blueberry Growers Need AgTech

 Washington is the nation’s leading producer of apples, pears and sweet cherries, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS). In 2025, the state grew about two-thirds of U.S. commercial apples, a crop valued at nearly $1.9 billion, along with about 70% of the nation’s sweet cherries and 44% of its pears. Washington also led the country in cultivated blueberries, producing 192.4 million pounds, about a quarter of the U.S. crop. Blueberries combine nearly every challenge Reservoir startups work on: a labor-intensive harvest that is hard to mechanize without damaging fruit, and constant disease and pest pressure.

 Those crops share a common constraint: labor. Labor represents 50% to 57% of orchard variable costs for Washington apples, according to WSU. H-2A guest worker positions certified in Washington nearly doubled between 2017 and 2025, to more than 34,500, according to the U.S. Department of Labor. Over a similar period, the number of Washington farms with orchards fell 12%, according to the USDA Census of Agriculture.

 “Our growers are spending more on inputs every season, and they will not adopt technology that was not developed or tested locally,” said Ines Hanrahan, executive director of the Washington Tree Fruit Research Commission. “A machine that hasn’t been through a Washington growing season isn’t ready for one. Building here, with growers involved from day one, is how we make sure our industry is robot ready, and the robots are ready for our industry.”

 Like Reservoir’s sites in Salinas, California’s Wine Country, and Arizona, Reservoir Farms – Washington is designed around a public-private partnership model that seeks to pair local research institutions, grower organizations and economic development groups with national industry partners. TRIDEC is providing financial support tying the site to the Tri-Cities region’s long-term economic development strategy. Reservoir’s multi-region model is also backed by John Deere, which committed $10 million over three years in August, and Western Growers, which announced a $1.5 million, three-year partnership earlier this year.

 “Agriculture is the heart and soul of this region, and the next generation of ag jobs will be in designing, running and servicing the technology,” said Karl Dye, president and CEO of TRIDEC. “Reservoir gives agricultural technology companies a reason to build here. That’s why TRIDEC is backing it with real dollars with the full support of our membership.”

translationZh:
Reservoir今日宣布推出Reservoir Farms – Washington，这是一个面向 rugged physical AI（ rugged physical AI）的全新农场技术社区，预计于2027年春季在华盛顿州雅基马谷开放。该地区高价值作物农业产值超过30亿美元。

该消息在FIRA USA上宣布。这是该公司在太平洋西北地区的首个社区，正与华盛顿果树研究委员会（WTFRC）、三城发展委员会（TRIDEC）、北美蓝莓委员会及其他国家和地方组织合作开发。Reservoir还在探索与华盛顿州立大学普罗瑟灌溉农业研究与推广中心（IAREC）的合作。这是Reservoir继亚利桑那州尤马之后在加州以外的第二次扩张，尤马项目是与亚利桑那大学的试点合作。

“技术对华盛顿农业的未来具有战略意义，”Reservoir创始人兼首席执行官Danny Bernstein表示。“果树、蓝莓、酿酒葡萄和啤酒花是世界上最难自动化的作物之一，而劳动力现在是华盛顿种植者面临的最大成本。向太平洋西北地区扩张表明Reservoir模式正在发挥作用。当你把开发者放到真实农场中，与愿意说真话的种植者在一起，rugged physical AI从原型到量产的速度会快得多。”

**Reservoir Farms – Washington如何支持Rugged Physical AI初创企业**

Reservoir Farms – Washington沿用Reservoir其他地点的相同合作模式，将初创企业安置在运营中的农场，与研究人员和种植者一起在商业条件下构建、测试和完善技术。初期工作将聚焦果树和蓝莓，并额外在酿酒葡萄和啤酒花中开展测试，计划随时间推移扩展到大田作物系统。

Reservoir已在各地点拥有30多家初创企业入驻，将为初创企业提供Reservoir Farms – Washington的多个进入通道。驻场初创企业将获得Reservoir会员的标准权益，准会员级初创企业将获得华盛顿的免费农场使用权。Bonsai Robotics和Sky Sense已在开发果树技术，早期初创企业Cordon和Rootline也将作为会员加入Reservoir Farms – Washington。

与领先研究机构的合作继续是Reservoir的战略重点，以确保生产力和劳动力成果得到同等考虑。为此，华盛顿州立大学和Reservoir正在探索建立合作夥伴关系的机会，重点推进农业创新、研究和技术开发。

“华盛顿种植者需要在真实农业条件下测试的创新技术，”WSU普罗瑟IAREC主任Naidu Rayapati博士表示。“将农业科技初创企业与我们的教职员工聚集在一起，在包括果园和葡萄园在内的多样化种植系统中评估新兴技术，可以在单个生长季内为种植者提供宝贵见解，并在多个季节进行严格验证，帮助他们做出明智决策、降低风险并提高生产力和盈利能力。”

**华盛顿果树和蓝莓种植者为何需要农业科技**

根据美国农业部国家农业统计局（NASS）的数据，华盛顿是美国苹果、梨和甜樱桃的领先生产州。2025年，该州生产了约三分之二的美国商业苹果，作物价值近19亿美元，以及约70%的美国甜樱桃和44%的梨。华盛顿还在栽培蓝莓方面领先全国，产量为1.924亿磅，约占美国作物的四分之一。蓝莓几乎汇集了Reservoir初创企业所应对的所有挑战：劳动密集型的采收难以在不损伤果实的情况下实现机械化，以及持续不断的病害和虫害压力。

这些作物有一个共同制约因素：劳动力。根据WSU的数据，劳动力占华盛顿苹果园可变成本的50%至57%。根据美国劳工部的数据，2017年至2025年间，华盛顿认证的H-2A客工岗位几乎翻了一番，达到超过34,500个。根据美国农业部农业普查，同期华盛顿拥有果园的农场数量下降了12%。

“我们的种植者每个季节在投入品上的支出都在增加，他们不会采用未在当地开发或测试的技术，”华盛顿果树研究委员会执行主任Ines Hanrahan表示。“一台没有经历过华盛顿生长季的机器还没有准备好迎接一个生长季。在这里建设，让种植者从第一天就参与其中，是我们确保行业为机器人做好准备、机器人也为行业做好准备的方式。”

与Reservoir在加州萨利纳斯、葡萄酒之乡和亚利桑那州的地点一样，Reservoir Farms – Washington围绕公私合作模式设计，旨在将当地研究机构、种植者组织和经济发展团体与全国行业伙伴配对。TRIDEC正在提供财政支持，将该站点与三城地区的长期经济发展战略联系起来。Reservoir的多区域模式还得到了约翰迪尔的支持，该公司在8月承诺三年内投入1000万美元；以及Western Growers的支持，后者今年早些时候宣布了一项150万美元的三年合作。

“农业是这个地区的核心和灵魂，下一代农业工作岗位将在于设计、运营和维护技术，”TRIDEC总裁兼首席执行官Karl Dye表示。“Reservoir为农业科技公司提供了在这里建设的理由。这就是为什么TRIDEC以真金白银支持它，并得到我们全体会员的全力支持。”
author: Matt Hopkins
contentHtml:
First Pacific Northwest site to open spring 2027, developed in collaboration the Washington Tree Fruit Research Commission and TRIDEC to put agricultural robotics startups in working orchards, vineyards and berry fields.
